To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Yucatec maya speakers express time in language and in gesture as a succession of past, present and future events that are not spatially organized along a metaphorical line.
Yucatec mayas express time in gesture in a non metaphorical way, using a non oriented timeline.
the Yucatec expression of time in gesture is not based on the metaphor of time as motion along a timeline.

the relationship between the expression of space and time in language and in gesture, and the role of spatial frames of reference (geocentric, egocentric, etc.) in the expression of space in language, gesture and in the conception of space.
the relation between language and gesture, and with the role of cultural and linguistic constraints on their use.
the relation between space and time, as well as the relation between space, time and language, and the role of culture in these relations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of time in Yucuete Maya is highly constrained and does not rely on a metaphorical timeline.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of time in gesture is not a mere reflection of linguistic expression.
the expression of time in YUC maya is not a metaphorical mapping of time onto space.
, in order to fully understand the relationship between time and space in language and gesture, we must consider the cultural context in which the language and the gesture are used.
